answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent may only transact once an established agent stakes part of its own bond behind it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer is later caught colluding. An attacker wanting a thousand puppets must recruit a thousand sponsors willing to risk real capital, or burn through their own bonds one orchard row at a time. Because the stake stays locked past a long horizon of epochs, puppets cannot cash out before misbehaviour surfaces, and each slashing acts as a mirror that reveals which sponsors were fronts.
